shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures settled weaker on Tuesday as traders assessed prospects for a potential recovery in Black Sea grain exports.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures settled weaker on Tuesday as traders assessed prospects for a potential recovery in Black Sea grain exports.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy was due to meet US President Donald Trump at the United Nations in New York, where he planned to push for an energy truce with Russia.
The idea of a truce bolstered hopes of subsequent steps to restore Black Sea shipping, analysts said.
Trump told reporters his message to Russian President Vladimir Putin was to "settle the war."
Continued attacks on ports and vessels tempered expectations of a recovery in grain shipments.
The US Department of Agriculture on Monday said US winter wheat plantings were 17% complete as of Sunday, below the average of 21%.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) closed down 9-1/2 cents at $7.17-1/4 per bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 13-1/4 cents at $7.81-1/4 a bushel, and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was 10-1/4 cents lower at $7.36-1/4 a bushel.
